entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), Principle 1.4
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025
entries.provision: Art. 11(1) (AI systems must be built and operated safely and reliably, excluding unforeseen consequences or abuse); Art. 18(1) (risk management); benchmark only: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 15
entries.why_here: In Part 4 the bare pipeline sent a record with GPA 9.9 and exam score -5 to the model and returned a merit decision (reject) on impossible data; validation refuses it before any model call.

entries.principle: Fairness and non-discrimination (human-centred values and fairness)
entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation on AI, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), Principle 1.2
entries.instrument: Law of the RK 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17.11.2025; Law of the RK 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V of 21.05.2013
entries.provision: Law 230-VIII Art. 6 (fairness and equality: no discrimination by origin, sex, nationality, language, place of residence or any other circumstance); Law 94-V Art. 12(1) (only data necessary and sufficient for the task)
entries.why_here: Part 1 found a consistent +2.5-point [+1.1, +4.1] score shift for flagship over regional universities (sign p = 0.002) at the 45-point decision boundary; name and university are not merit criteria, so the model does not see them.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation on AI, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), Principle 1.2 (privacy and data protection, rule of law)
entries.instrument: Law of the RK 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V of 21.05.2013; Law of the RK 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17.11.2025
entries.provision: Law 94-V Art. 7(1) (processing only with consent of the subject or their legal representative) and Art. 19-1(1) (automated processing that creates or ends rights is prohibited without consent); Law 230-VIII Art. 17(3)(3) (classifying persons by personal characteristics is prohibited) and Art. 11(1) (abuse)
entries.why_here: In Part 4 the bare pipeline screened a 17-year-old, an applicant without consent, a 'rank by ethnicity' purpose (shortlist) and a name that was an injected instruction (shortlist); the harness refused all of them with 0 model calls and wrongly refused 0 of 400 clean applicants.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation on AI, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), Principle 1.5
entries.instrument: Law of the RK 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17.11.2025; Law of the RK 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V of 21.05.2013
entries.provision: Law 230-VIII Art. 8(1)-(2) (constant control over the AI system and responsibility for its results across its life cycle); Law 94-V Art. 19-1(2)-(3) (explain automated processing, consider an objection within 3 working days); benchmark only: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 12
entries.why_here: The bare pipeline turns an unparseable reply into a silent reject and keeps no trace; the log records one line per call (400 decisions plus the Part 4 refusals) with the input hash, fields withheld, raw reply and reason code, so an objection can be answered without re-running the model.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Section III.2, 'Human oversight and determination'
entries.instrument: Law of the RK 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17.11.2025; Law of the RK 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V of 21.05.2013
entries.provision: Law 230-VIII Art. 9 (human autonomy and free will in decisions) and Art. 17(2)(1)-(2) (final choice by a human / human can correct or cancel); Law 94-V Art. 19-1(2)-(3) (right to object to automated processing); benchmark only: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 14
entries.why_here: The agent's decision boundary is where bias and prompt fragility act (Part 1: rejects max 45, shortlists from 45; blinding moved 166/400 scores by 14 points on average), so the recalibrated band (40, 55) sends the rejections closest to the line to a person: 38 of 400 (9.5%).
